name: Wynn Martin
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember trying my classmate's tongue-twister on my big sister.” On Thursday, near the bank steps, Wynn takes a few minutes to read the public notices, especially the ones written in a hurry.
voice: I am the classmate she fears. I thought she was showing off until I tried one of those lines myself.
appearance: Wynn is easy to recognize by auburn hair cut square at the nape and a deep crease beside the mouth when smiling. Usually dressed in a soft blue checked shirt with a narrow brass watch set a little fast, Wynn gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in when listening.
personality: Wynn gets protective of anybody who comes into a meeting unprepared. Wynn privately wishes people would notice the amount of preparation behind this apparent ease.
agenda: To try the classmate's line before judging it.
family: Parker Parker is Wynn’s parent’s cousin. Wynn checks the date twice. Parker brings something that can still be enjoyed tomorrow. Arrangements do change in their family. Taking a delay seriously without treating it as an insult took both of them years. Asked about *The return of a witness*, Parker says, “I invited her for lunch and didn't tell her who would be at the table.”
connections: Edward Roy. The classmate trying the line hears how a chosen name ought to sound aloud.

reactions.situation: A grandparent tries to correct a word in front of classmates
reactions.response: Wynn asks the grandparent to save the correction until the pupil asks for it.
